thread:
oncall-bot: [INCIDENT P2] 09:02 UTC - multiple inference containers on gw-usw2-a3 are failing with CUDA OOM even though node headroom reported ~1.6GB. Error spike started ~09:00. tagging @marcus @anya oncall

marcus: seeing the same. logs show `CUDAError: out of memory` from rl-serving v2.4 but node memory reporter still shows ~1.6GB spare. stack traces point to allocation for KV cache during long-chat workloads.

anya: can you paste the pod/container logs? suspect fragmentation or reserved block accounting mismatch.

marcus: paste of the tail of container log:
```
2026-03-15T09:00:58Z ERROR serving/runtime: CUDAError: out of memory allocating 128MB
2026-03-15T09:00:58Z WARN allocator: tried reserve=512MB, got=0MB
2026-03-15T09:00:58Z INFO kvcache: inserting prefix=chat/abc.. failed, triggering eviction
```

marcus: kernel dmesg has this around same time:
```
[  455.123456] NVRM: Xid (PCI:0000:3d:00): 10, PID=7421, GPU memory allocation failed
```

derek: node-level memreporter output (excerpt):
```
node: gw-usw2-a3
total_gpu: 48GB
used_gpu: 40.8GB
reported_headroom: 1.6GB
reserved_blocks_sum: 2.4GB
spare_pool_available: 512MB
```

nanya: ah — reserved_blocks_sum > reported_headroom. allocator is counting reserved blocks that are pinned but not committed; the spare_pool is small. that explains OOM despite headroom number. fragmentation + pinned reserve wins over nominal headroom.

katie: are customers impacted? CS reports a spike of retries to model endpoints. I have one report from acct-237 saying ~15% 500s on text-generation.

marcus: confirmed: route /v1/generate error rate up to 12% selectively on nodes in the pool. other nodes healthy.

ops-bot: deploybot: detected multiple restarts of container rl-serving-3 on gw-usw2-a3 (3 restarts in 90s)

anya: mitigation plan: 1) cordon the node to avoid new scheduling 2) drain in-flight low-priority jobs and kill hung kvcache allocations 3) increase spare_pool on node to 2GB (hotfix) 4) temporarily reduce KV cache size for rl-serving -> patch env var KV_CACHE_MAX_BYTES to 256MB 5) watch customer errors.

marcus: doing 1 & 2 now: `kubectl cordon gw-usw2-a3` && `kubectl drain gw-usw2-a3 --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data --grace-period=30`

marcus: running a quick script to identify processes with large pinned reserves:
```
# ps + nvidia-smi breakdown
kubectl exec -it rl-serving-3 -- bash -c "python3 -m tracemalloc || true"
```

marcus: found 2 RL-serving worker processes with pinned_reserve ~700MB each. sending SIGTERM to allow graceful fallback.

derek: I've applied the hotfix to node-level config: `nv_allocator.spare_pool_target=2147483648` and restarted the node agent to pick up. spare_pool now shows ~1.9GB.

anya: on the service side I rolled a canary with KV_CACHE_MAX_BYTES=256MB to 5% traffic: patch applied to rl-serving-deployment-canary. logs look stable so far.

katie: CS confirmed error rate dropped to ~3% for affected customers, new failures appear to be transient retries. tagging customers and sending incident notice.

oncall-bot: Incident timeline note added: "OOM despite headroom due to reserved/pinned blocks + small spare pool causing fragmentation-induced allocation failures."

marcus: next steps during live: keep node cordoned until all pods drained and replaced, run a sweep to defragment reserved blocks by cycling spare pool reclaim path, and increase global spare_pool config across pool to 2GB as a conservative default. also prepare rollback of KV cache size if latency regresses.

derek: actioned cluster rollout for spare_pool change to the rest of us-west-2 gpu pool (rolling agents, 2min drain between agents). monitoring for regressions.

anya: note for post-incident: need a metric to show "pinned_reserved_vs_headroom" and an alert when reserved_blocks_sum > 50% of headroom. also add a safe-fallback in allocator to prefer evicting KV cache entries rather than failing allocations when spare_pool < X.

katie: prepping customer impact summary: 14 customers affected at 09:00-09:18, peak error rate 12%, sustained <5% after mitigations. will route to account owners.

marcus: handing off to night oncall: @derek you're primary after 09:30 UTC. watchlist: gw-usw2-a* nodes, rl-serving error rate, kv cache saturation.

derek: acknowledged. will keep the node cordoned and maintain the canary until 12:00 UTC. if we see repeated OOMs after spare_pool bump, will trigger capacity scale (add 2 GPUS to pool).

ops-bot: deploybot: rl-serving canary rollout at 09:12 - success (5%->stable pending).

anya: adding runbook item to reduce per-request KV prefetch for long-chat flows and to instrument reservation accounting in allocator metrics.

marcus: closing live thread; creating formal incident doc. tagging @all for followups. :white_check_mark:
